notes.summary: Intrinsic comparison of actual H/CPSH/PSH for all Reeb fields, with normalized quotient cocycles and uniform pointwise bounds. E1 preservation and strong-topology continuity remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The orbit-root construction is presentation independent and gives order isomorphisms between the actual FS, continuous-psh and decreasing-net PSH classes, including irrational and nonproportional fields. It preserves decreasing limits, zero sets and minus-infinite loci. Normalizing by the value at the trivial valuation gives a genuine map on constant quotients; the unnormalized map does not descend. Continuity is proved for local uniform convergence on CPSH and full pointwise convergence on PSH, not Wu's weaker quasi-monomial topology or the finite-energy strong topology. Compact-slice constants depend only on fixed algebra generators and Reeb fields.
notes.text:
Work on the fixed carrier K=X0^T. The premises are the torified action and actual H/CPSH/PSH definitions in Wu2406.13684v1, respectively LF lines 218–246, 277–286, 344–345 and 762–764. All subsequent comparison arguments here are intrinsic and do not use a filtration-energy identification.

Choose homogeneous algebra generators h_i of the maximal ideal, with weights beta_i, and write d_xi(alpha)=<xi,alpha>. Every supported weight is a nonnegative integral combination of the beta_i. Consequently c=min_i d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i) and C=max_i d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i) bound the degree ratio for every supported weight, independently of FS presentations and assigned weights.

The torified action is (v+t eta)(sum f_alpha)=min_alpha(v(f_alpha)+t d_eta(alpha)). The canonical reference is rho_xi(v)=max_i[-v(h_i)/d_xi(beta_i)]. Its orbit section v+rho_xi(v)xi lies in K. Thus every xi-equivariant potential satisfies u(v)=u(v+rho_xi(v)xi)+rho_xi(v), and its restriction to K determines it everywhere after torification. K is compact: it is the closed torified subset of the coordinate unit polydisc satisfying min_i v(h_i)=0.

This reference also agrees with zero-weight primary FS presentations. If (f_j) is primary, some power of the maximal ideal is contained in it. At v in K, choose h_i of value zero. If every f_j had positive value, an expression of h_i^r in that ideal would have positive value, since all regular coefficients have nonnegative value on K. This is impossible. Hence some f_j has value zero, so the zero-weight presentation vanishes on K and equals rho_xi by equivariance.

For every actual PSH potential and t>=0, the FS inequalities pass through both completions to give u(v)-Ct <= u(v+t eta) <= u(v)-ct. Reverse-orbit inequalities follow as well. If u(v) is finite, this orbit function is finite, Lipschitz, strictly decreasing and surjective onto R. Define R_xi,eta u(v) as its unique zero parameter. If u(v)=-infinity, the entire orbit is -infinity; define the image value to be -infinity.

For an FS presentation, this construction gives exactly R_xi,eta[max_j(lambda_j-v(f_j))/d_xi(alpha_j)]=max_j(lambda_j-v(f_j))/d_eta(alpha_j). Since the definition uses the function's orbit zero, it is independent of the presentation. It gives actual H membership. Order follows from decreasing orbit functions. For CPSH potentials, ||R u-R w||_K <= ||u-w||_K/c: source differences bounded on K are bounded everywhere by equivariance, and the lower slope bound controls the displacement of roots. Uniform FS approximation therefore proves target CPSH membership.

For a defining decreasing CPSH net u_a decreasing to u, roots decrease. At a finite root r, the evaluations at v+(r-epsilon)eta and v+(r+epsilon)eta have opposite signs, eventually also for u_a. Their roots therefore converge to r. At a minus-infinite point, evaluation at v-M eta eventually becomes negative for every M, forcing roots below -M. This proves target PSH membership and preservation of decreasing limits. The same bracket argument proves continuity for arbitrary nets converging pointwise at all analytic points.

The image has the same zero set and minus-infinite locus as u. Taking roots along a third Reeb field proves R_eta,zeta R_xi,eta=R_xi,zeta; taking the third field to be xi proves the inverse. Thus these are order isomorphisms. For a fixed CPSH potential, varying the target Reeb field also gives local uniform continuity: roots are uniformly bounded on compact sets, orbit points range in a compact set, and the lower slope bound is uniform.

For every actual PSH potential, sup_K u=u(v_triv) is finite. This follows first for FS, then CPSH, then decreasing limits; a minus-infinite value at v_triv would force the potential identically minus infinity. Normalize by N_xi u=u-u(v_triv). The root image of a normalized potential is already normalized. Therefore [u] maps to [R_xi,eta(N_xi u)] independently of representatives, with inverse and cocycle. The raw map does not descend: for k[x,y], xi=(1,1), eta=(1,2), the difference R(rho_xi+2)-rho_eta equals 2 at v_triv and 1 at the monomial valuation (3,0).

For normalized nonpositive potentials, u/c <= R u <= u/C. With delta=max_i|log(d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i))|, this gives |R u-u| <= (exp(delta)-1)(-u) at finite points of K. On a compact Reeb slice, delta is bounded by a fixed multiple of ||eta-xi||. For any fixed probability measure mu, the tail integral of -R u above A is at most c^(-1) times the tail integral of -u above cA. This does not control moving MA measures. Actual energy monotonicity and translation additionally give -B/c <= E_eta(R u) <= 0 when -B <= u <= 0 on K; this oscillation bound is insufficient for families bounded only in energy.

The complete argument is in Sections 1–2 of P13.1-argument.md and P13.1-paper.tex. The finite program checks include 832 orbit examples, including infinite semivaluation coordinates. These checks are observations, not the proof. No E1 preservation or continuity in the quasi-monomial/strong topologies is claimed.

notes.summary: Signed finite-type norms represent primary FS lists exactly on compact Reeb slices and satisfy uniform signed cutoff estimates. The cutoff means are not identified with general genuine cone energy.
notes.detailedSummary: An explicit quotient filtration handles relations, saturation and arbitrary signed generator weights. Primary lists can be supplemented with sufficiently negative algebra generators without changing any potential on a compact Reeb slice. Valid degree shifts establish signed cutoff convergence without negating a multiplicative norm. For nonpositive weights, the limiting negative cutoff means vary within exp(±(2n+1)delta), with constants independent of weights and potentials. The argument does not establish presentation independence of the cutoff mean as a potential functional or its equality with genuine affine-cone energy.
notes.text:
Use the carrier, equivariance and degree-ratio constants proved in n1. Let g_i be homogeneous algebra generators, permitting redundant elements, with arbitrary real assigned weights lambda_i. Define F^a R_alpha as the span of monomials g^e of homogeneous weight alpha whose assigned weight sum e_i lambda_i is at least a. Define chi(f) as its largest filtration index, and extend over homogeneous components by minima.

There are only finitely many eligible monomials in a fixed weight space: a positive Reeb degree bounds their exponent sum. Thus the index is finite and attained, the filtration is left continuous, exhaustive and separated, and chi(fg)>=chi(f)+chi(g). Relations are retained through the spanning construction. Every homogeneous norm value lies between min_i(lambda_i/d_xi(wt g_i))d_xi(alpha) and max_i(lambda_i/d_xi(wt g_i))d_xi(alpha).

Actual generator weights may exceed assigned weights. Replacing all lambda_i by chi(g_i) leaves the filtration unchanged. One inclusion follows from chi(g_i)>=lambda_i; the other follows from multiplicativity, which bounds every expression's minimum actual monomial weight by chi(f). An expression attaining the old index therefore also attains it with the actual weights. This verifies Wu2106.13395v2 Definition 3.6, including norm saturation.

The exact norm/potential correspondence is sup_{f homogeneous nonzero}(chi(f)-v(f))/d_xi(wt f)=max_i(lambda_i-v(g_i))/d_xi(wt g_i). For the upper bound, take an expression attaining chi(f), use the valuation inequality on its sum, and divide each monomial expression by its common degree. It becomes a weighted average of generator expressions. For the lower bound use f=g_i and chi(g_i)>=lambda_i. Infinite valuation values cause no exception.

For a primary FS list f_j, append fixed algebra generators h_i with weight -M. On K, some f_j has value zero by n1, so the original potentials have a uniform lower bound -B over any compact Reeb slice Q. Choosing M>=B max_{xi in Q,i}d_xi(beta_i) puts all appended terms below that bound. The potentials are exactly unchanged on K and hence everywhere by equivariance, simultaneously for every field in Q. M may depend on the potential; comparison constants do not. Rational assigned weights give a finitely generated integer Rees algebra after clearing denominators, generated over k[t] by g_i t^(-ell_i). Filtered spanning expressions prove this even with relations and negative weights. No integer Noetherian Rees assertion is made for irrational weights.

Negation is invalid: assigning x and x^2 weight -1 in k[x] gives chi(x)=chi(x^2)=-1. Negation violates multiplicativity because 1<1+1. The valid shift is chi_{A,beta}(f)=chi(f)+A d_beta(alpha) on R_alpha. Every expression receives the same degree shift, so this is exactly the quotient filtration with shifted generator weights. For sufficiently large A it is nonnegative, multiplicative, finite type and linearly bounded, with F^0R=R.

Let N_xi(m) be the cutoff dimension, W_xi^chi(m) the sum of its spectral weights, and D_xi^beta(m)=sum_{d_xi(alpha)<=m}d_beta(alpha)dim R_alpha. The finite identity W_xi^{chi_{A,beta}}(m)=W_xi^chi(m)+A D_xi^beta(m) holds before taking limits. The cone volume theorem in Wu2106.13395v2 applies to the normal good cone and gives N_xi(m)~V_xi m^n/n!. Stieltjes summation gives D_xi^xi(m)=mN_xi(m)-integral_0^m N_xi(t)dt, hence D_xi^xi(m)/(mN_xi(m))->n/(n+1).

Apply that source's Corollary 3.13 only to the explicitly nonnegative shifted filtration chi_{A,xi}; all its filtration and boundedness hypotheses have been checked. Combining its convergence with the finite shift identity and the established degree limit proves signed convergence S_chi(xi)=lim W_xi^chi(m)/(mN_xi(m)). Its own-degree shift adds A n/(n+1). This is not subtraction of unproved limits.

When all assigned weights are nonpositive, all spectral weights are nonpositive. The cutoff inclusions from n1 give W_xi(m/c)<=W_eta(m)<=W_xi(m/C). Passing through the established limits yields (V_xi/V_eta)c^(-(n+1))S_chi(xi)<=S_chi(eta)<=(V_xi/V_eta)C^(-(n+1))S_chi(xi). The dimension inclusions give V_xi/C^n<=V_eta<=V_xi/c^n. Therefore exp(-(2n+1)delta)(-S_chi(xi))<=-S_chi(eta)<=exp((2n+1)delta)(-S_chi(xi)). This includes zero means without division and applies to irrational nonproportional fields.

Normalized primary FS potentials admit nonpositive-weight representations: subtract their trivial-valuation value times the source degree from each weight, then append sufficiently negative generators. At least one retained weight is zero, and the same weights give normalized orbit images at all other fields. Rational perturbations bounded by epsilon times generator degree alter each weight-space spectral value by at most epsilon times that degree, so the limiting means differ by at most epsilon n/(n+1); potentials differ uniformly by at most epsilon.

An own-degree shift translates the genuine potential by A, whose genuine energy translates by A. Thus any universal representation E=a_n S would necessarily have a_n=(n+1)/n. A shift by source degree is not a constant shift at a nonproportional target field, so cancellation at both fields is unjustified. Neither the universal energy representation nor presentation independence of S as a potential functional is proved here.

Details are in Sections 3–4 of P13.1-argument.md. Rerun the finite observations with python checks.py. They include 52 primary supplementation examples, exact signed shift identities, and finite cutoff inclusions. At cutoff 160, the example means are -323/644 for xi=(1,1) and -325/972 for eta=(1,2); these are finite observations rather than analytic-energy evidence.

notes.summary: Actual mixed-MA and energy continuity is proved for locally uniformly convergent CPSH sequences with varying Reeb fields. Translation disproves the printed E=S normalization; the corrected factor is established for actual projective test configurations.
notes.detailedSummary: CLD's continuous-psh sheaf, weighted-current continuity, structural theorem, smooth cutoff and density results yield genuine bounded analytic convergence on the common carrier, including irrational limits. The proof retains n−1 potential factors, one radial factor and denominator nV. Separately, BHJ's filtration, DH barycenter and intersection-energy results establish E_projective=(n+1)S_cumulative/n for actual ample projective test configurations over normal varieties, with signed weights. Neither result supplies the general weighted cone-to-projective energy bridge or unbounded finite-energy limits.
notes.text:
Use n1's intrinsic reference and n2's degree inclusions. Suppose xi_l->xi and u_{i,l} in CPSH(xi_l) converge locally uniformly away from the vertex to u_i in CPSH(xi). Then the actual mixed probability measures converge weakly on K. If u_l similarly converges to u, then E_xi_l(u_l)->E_xi(u). These are sequence/local-uniform conclusions.

Here is the checked CLD application. The reference functions rho_xi_l converge locally uniformly by n1's root parameter-continuity argument, as do their maxima with zero. The volume inclusions prove V_xi_l->V_xi>0. FS functions are locally uniform limits of smooth psh functions by Wu2406.13684v1, LF318–319. CLD1204.6277v2 Definition 8.1.7 and Proposition 8.1.9 preserve continuous-psh membership under local uniform limits, so actual CPSH functions satisfy the relevant CLD hypothesis; positivity of a distribution alone is not used as a converse criterion.

The analytification away from the vertex is separated, pure-dimensional and boundaryless. CLD Theorem 15.7.1 supplies its calibrated tropical structure and local differential separation without a smoothness assumption. The positive closed radial currents T_l=dd^c max(rho_xi_l,0) converge by distributional differentiation. Apply CLD Proposition 8.7.2 with T_l and exactly n−1 continuous psh potential factors. For n=1 use its q=0 case. This proves convergence of the actual mixed top currents.

Their support is the common compact K. For CPSH this follows by uniform FS approximation on K, equivariance giving local uniform approximation everywhere, and the same CLD argument starting with Wu's FS probability theorem. CLD Corollary 6.2.4 provides a compactly supported smooth cutoff equal to one near K, so the mass calculation and division by V_l are legitimate. Continuous tests on K follow from extending them to a compact neighborhood and CLD Corollary 6.2.6's smooth approximation; probability mass bounds the approximation errors.

The actual energy is E_xi(u)=(nV_xi)^(-1) sum_{j=0}^{n-1} integral (u-rho_xi)(dd^c u)^j(dd^c rho_xi)^(n−1−j)dd^c rho_xi^+. Apply the weighted form of Proposition 8.7.2 to each summand, with continuous zeroth weight u_l-rho_xi_l, the corresponding n−1 potential factors, and radial T_l. Test against the common cutoff and divide by nV_l. This proves genuine energy convergence while retaining the moving weight. It applies in particular to rational approximants of n1's orbit image of a fixed CPSH potential. It supplies no unbounded decreasing-net tail estimate.

The normalization can be checked directly. The actual mixed measures have mass one under Wu2406.13684v1 Theorem 2.12. Substituting rho_xi+a in the energy formula leaves the currents unchanged and gives E_xi(rho_xi+a)=a. For k[x_1,...,x_n], xi=(1,...,1), and the degree norm, the associated potential is rho_xi+1. At every integer cutoff m>=1, N(m)=binomial(m+n,n) and W(m)=n binomial(m+n,n+1), so W(m)/(mN(m))=n/(n+1), whereas genuine energy equals 1. For k[x,y] these values are 2/3 and 1. This is an exact counterexample to the printed unmodified E=S equality, not a numerical inference.

For n=1 on k[x] with d_xi(x)=a, V=1/a and the calibrated radial slope jump has mass 1/a at v(x)=0. The normalized measure is one Dirac mass; the empty potential product and denominator V give translation energy c. The cumulative degree-shift coefficient remains 1/2.

An exact corrected representation is available for actual projective test configurations. Let Z be normal projective of dimension n−1, A ample, and (Zcal,Acal) an ample test configuration. After the sufficiently divisible section-ring normalization in BHJ1504.06568v3 Proposition 2.15, Proposition 5.9 identifies degree-wise filtration measures with DH. Signed weights have uniformly compact normalized support, so their means converge. Proposition 3.12(iii) identifies the mean with (Acal_bar^n)/(n A^(n−1)); Definition 7.2 identifies this intersection number with the actual projective energy. Thus the mean/energy equality is established by an intersection formula, not merely a distribution theorem.

Take a normal determination by normalizing the graph dominating the model and product. Pullbacks retain the metric and intersection numbers; BHJ Theorem 3.14 retains DH under normalization since Z is reduced. Section 6.7's mixed model measures have mass one. Vertical coefficients r_E evaluate as r_E/b_E, so Remark 6.12 and Lemma 7.4 recover the n-term energy formula with denominator nV. There is no further division by V after integrating a probability measure.

Writing N_d=h^0(Z,dA), W_d its signed total weight, the degree-wise convergence gives W_d/(dN_d)->e. Hilbert asymptotics and summation yield sum_{d<=m}W_d/[m sum_{d<=m}N_d]->n e/(n+1): bound the tail error by epsilon dN_d and discard the fixed initial sum after normalization. Therefore E_projective=(n+1)S_cumulative/n in this precise projective scope. Normality suffices; smoothness is not assumed. This does not prove the weighted cone radial/Veronese bridge for arbitrary primary FS norms.

The detailed analytic application, normalization proof and projective application are in Sections 5–6 of P13.1-argument.md and the standalone P13.1-paper.tex.

notes.summary: P13.1 remains unresolved: genuine finite-energy comparison, moving-MA tails and uniform differentiation are missing. Source audit, preserved inputs and a twice-compiled 13-page paper are delivered.
notes.detailedSummary: The final status is partial. The main indispensable gaps are the general signed cone-energy representation with calibrated weighted quotient factors, energy-range estimates and E1 preservation, moving mixed-measure integrability, a justified envelope dependency chain on singular quotients, and actual two-sign uniform energy differentiation. The source audit records the energy-factor inconsistency, growth-convention mismatch and regularizability dependency without claiming that the newer envelope theorem is false. Eight supplied source hashes and 55 literal excerpts were checked; the final paper compiled twice, with no warnings on the second pass.
notes.text:
The results in n1–n3 do not complete unchanged P13.1. The explicit remaining mathematical obligations are:

1. Identify the genuine cone CLD energy intrinsically with an appropriate signed norm representation for every primary FS presentation, including all weighted quotient, Veronese, radial and calibrated finite-degree factors. The bounded irrational passage in n3 is available once the rational representation is established; it does not prove that representation.
2. Obtain a normalized genuine-energy estimate controlled by source energy, uniformly on compact Reeb slices, and use it to preserve E1 through defining decreasing nets. The oscillation estimate and algebraic cutoff estimate do not supply this.
3. Prove the mixed-integrability and vanishing tails required for moving measures such as MA_eta((R u_a)^[j],rho_eta^[n−1−j]) tested against the unbounded target potentials, including limits in which the field varies. A fixed-measure tail comparison is insufficient.
4. Establish the actual extended/enveloped-energy functional, its agreement with the genuine operator, and both-sign uniform differentiation in a proved dense direction class. Continuous directions require genuine uniform approximation; no quadratic estimate for every continuous direction is asserted. Strong finite-energy topology and Wu's quasi-monomial PSH topology are also not covered by the proved continuity statements.

The decisive literal source audit is as follows. Wu2106.13395v2 Lemma 3.16(b) states S=n/(n+1) times the degree-wise mean; its final Theorem 5.15 proof writes E=degree-wise mean=S. The degree example in n3 contradicts the latter under the printed definitions. Proposition 5.13 uses mL sections while its moment-coordinate radial expression drops the displayed 1/m coefficient; a valid replacement must track the fiber map's degree and calibration. A nonvanishing section of mL does not trivialize L. Boucksom–Jonsson1805.11160v1 Theorem 4.13 has a smooth-projective standing hypothesis, explicitly at LF525, so it is not applied unchanged to singular normal quotients. BHJ supplies the projective result in n3 but does not automatically supply the missing cone bridge.

Lyuhui Wu2609.27610v1 Definition 3.15 uses lower growth g<=u+O(1), whereas Definition 6.1 uses upper growth u<=g+O(1). Log|z| distinguishes these conventions because FS functions there have a finite constant floor. The consistent convention recorded in this audit is upper growth. Correcting the sign alone does not justify the application: Proposition 4.19 invokes Lemma 3.25(1), whose explicit hypothesis already includes membership in the regularizable logarithmic class that Proposition 4.19 seeks to prove. This dependency propagates through Proposition 6.2(2), Theorem 6.3's smooth starting case and singular induction, Theorem 6.5 and Theorem 7.1. No noncircular replacement is proved here, and that theorem is not used as an indispensable premise. This is not a claim that it is false or an objection to its v1 status. Its countability-removal stage and the residual torus, global reference, quotient class and carrier applications also remain to be justified for a cone use.

The complete deliverables are P13.1-argument.md, P13.1-paper.tex and P13.1-paper.pdf. The final PDF has 13 pages. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps and records status partial. input.json is unchanged and byte-identical to input-original.json, with SHA256 6bef40f554a98298d3b9f8d21d1b38f373d390dd5443853613b2fbc4f1cf3656. assignment-original.txt preserves the decoded assignment verbatim; task-original.json preserves the raw task-object JSON bytes from the input.
